source: arXiv:2507.07107 + QuantBuffet TOM futures study (2025) + internal synthesis
title: H205 TOM Calendar Overlay on BAB — Backtest Design Finalized
summary: arXiv:2507.07107 (Du 2025) demonstrates that cross-sectional ML factor strategies on 500-1000 stocks benefit substantially from bias correction and cross-sectional neutralization, validating the design choice in H205 of using sector-neutral BAB (H192-D) as the base. Critically, the QuantBuffet TOM-futures study (2026-05-17 scan) showed 50%+ of momentum returns concentrated in a 3-day TOM window — the strongest precedent for H205's hypothesis that BAB alpha similarly concentrates in TOM windows. Combined with H201 confirming TOM on SPY OOS Sharpe 0.740, the H205 design is well-supported: hold H192-D positions during TOM window (last 2 + first 2 trading days), hold BIL otherwise. Confirm gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.5 (vs H192-D baseline 1.367). The QuantBuffet result provides a theoretical bridge: if institutional cash flows at month-end drive both TOM returns AND temporarily boost low-beta stocks (reduced leverage constraints, easier positioning), then the overlay mechanism is economically grounded.
actionable: Create backtesting/daily/run_h205.py implementing the TOM overlay on H192-D. Script should: (1) load H192-D signal logic (sector-neutral BAB, 30-stock universe, monthly rebalance), (2) apply TOM mask (last 2 + first 2 trading days), (3) hold H192-D portfolio on TOM days, BIL on non-TOM days, (4) report OOS Sharpe vs H192-D baseline. IS: 2013-2020, OOS: 2021-2026. Success gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.5.
